name: Portland
summary: Working waterfront, lighthouses, and arguably the best food per square mile in America.
seasonalTip: Early October: the harbor is still open for cruises and the crowds have gone home.

lodging.name: The Press Hotel
lodging.blurb: The old Portland Press Herald building — newsroom bones, typewriter details in the lobby.

foodMustTry.name: Brown-butter lobster roll at Eventide Oyster Co.
foodMustTry.blurb: The one that changed what a lobster roll could be. Served on a steamed bao-style bun.

foodMustTry.name: A donut from The Holy Donut
foodMustTry.blurb: Made with Maine potato. Sounds wrong, tastes right.

days.label: Day 5 — Lighthouses & the Old Port
days.summary: Sunrise at the most painted lighthouse in America, then eat your way through the Old Port.

item.title: Sunrise at Portland Head Light

location.name: Portland Head Light, Fort Williams Park
location.address: 12 Captain Strout Cir, Cape Elizabeth, ME

item.blurb: Commissioned by George Washington, lit since 1791, and the single most photographed lighthouse in the country. Go at sunrise and it's yours alone.

item.title: Lobster roll at Eventide Oyster Co.
item.blurb: Brown butter, warm bun, a dozen oysters on ice off the granite trough. Expect a wait; it's worth it.

item.title: Wander the Old Port
item.blurb: Cobblestones, ship chandlers turned bookshops, and a harbor that still works for a living.

days.label: Day 6 — Casco Bay
days.summary: Out on the water with the mail boat, back on land for art.

item.title: Casco Bay mail boat run
item.blurb: Ride along as the ferry delivers mail to the island communities — the cheapest, most local boat tour in New England.

item.title: Portland Museum of Art
item.blurb: Winslow Homer's Maine, plus the Wyeths — the coast you just stood on, painted.

item.title: Potato donuts at The Holy Donut
item.blurb: Dense, glazed, faintly savory. Get the dark chocolate sea salt and one maple bacon for the road.

days.label: Day 7 — Drive up the coast to Acadia
days.summary: Three hours north, but only if you refuse to stop. You will stop.

commute.scenicNote: US-1 through Camden and Belfast is the postcard route; I-95 is an hour faster and worth nothing.

stopsAlongWay.title: Camden Hills State Park
stopsAlongWay.blurb: Drive to the top of Mount Battie for the harbor view that put Camden on every calendar.

stopsAlongWay.title: Red's Eats, Wiscasset
stopsAlongWay.blurb: A roadside shack with a famous line and a full lobster's worth of meat in every roll.
